label: Reframed Habermasian discourse ethics around the embodied "concrete other"
description: Seyla Benhabib corrected the abstract rationalism of Habermas's universalization principle by introducing the "concrete other," demanding that communicative ethics attend to situated gender, narrative history, and relational needs.
dialecticalTension: Reconciles universalizable moral validity with feminist ethics of care and particularity.
historicalContext: Critique, Norm, and Utopia (1986) and Situating the Self (1992).

label: Converted Arendt's "right to have rights" into cosmopolitan democratic iterations
description: In The Reluctant Modernism of Hannah Arendt (1996) and The Rights of Others (2004), Benhabib turned Arendt's critique of statelessness into a juridical-political theory of migrant citizenship and porous democratic borders.
dialecticalTension: Mediates tension between bounded democratic self-determination and universal cosmopolitan hospitality.
historicalContext: Late-20th/early-21st-century Critical Theory and migration ethics.

citations.author: Seyla Benhabib
citations.work: The Rights of Others: Aliens, Residents, and Citizens

label: Debated normative agency vs. post-structuralist dissolution of the subject
description: In Feminist Contentions (1995), Benhabib challenged Judith Butler's performativity theory, arguing that strong post-structuralist death-of-the-subject claims undermine normative feminist accounts of agency and critical emancipation.
dialecticalTension: Canonical exchange between Frankfurt School critical universalism and post-structuralist performativity.
